definitions.explanation: the phase of the moon when it is not visible from Earth because it is positioned between Earth and the sun

examples.japanese: {新月|しんげつ}の{夜|よる}は{星|ほし}がよく{見|み}える。
examples.english: On new moon nights, you can see the stars well.

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}は{新月|しんげつ}なので{月|つき}は{見|み}えない。
examples.english: Since today is a new moon, you can't see the moon.

examples.japanese: {新月|しんげつ}から{満月|まんげつ}まで{約|やく}2{週間|しゅうかん}かかる。
examples.english: It takes about two weeks from new moon to full moon.

notes:
MOON PHASES:
- {新月|しんげつ} (new moon) - moon not visible
- {三日月|みかづき} (crescent moon)
- {上弦|じょうげん}の{月|つき} (first quarter moon)
- {満月|まんげつ} (full moon)
- {下弦|かげん}の{月|つき} (last quarter moon)

FORMATION:
{新|しん} (new) + {月|げつ} (moon) → new moon

ASTRONOMY NOTE:
During a {新月|しんげつ}, the moon is between Earth and the sun, so the illuminated side faces away from Earth. This is also the time when solar eclipses can occur.
